text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
***GENERAL***
ALL PAPERS
- Hungary will have a fully professional army within eight to 10 years and military service would be gradually phased out, Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti said.
- The union Workers' Council has withdrawn from an agreement on social insurance authority delegates.
- Hungary does not plan to to suspend diplomatic ties with Bosnia's Budapest embassy.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The head of Hungary's Intelligence Office said agents are underpaid even compared with other public service sectors.
***BUSINESS***
ALL PAPERS
- Agricultural producer prices dropped 3.7 percent in June month-on-month.
Tourism revenues in the January-July period at 739 million forints were 30 percent higher than expected.
- Hungary will get a 15-year loan of $18 million from the World Bank to overhaul healthcare.
- The BUX index of the Budapest Stock Exchange hit a new high of 8,168.13 points in record turnover 21.8 billion forints.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- An Industry Ministry study said that in the first stage of foreign direct investment machinery imports go up and are not matched by exports for a few years.
- Ford Hungary has challenged a police decision to buy Opel cars after a public procurement tender in which Ford also bid.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Hungary's per capita foreign debt dropped to $2,300 from $2,700 last year.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The loser of the national TV concession, Centyral European Media Enterprises plans to launch a commercial programme to be broadcast on of the Eutelsat satellites.
- Tesco supermarkets will be open on the August 20 holiday despite labour regulations.
